headline: Permits and Shuttles Required for Zion and Angels Landing
reservation: Zion National Park requires a shuttle for the main canyon drive for most of the year; tickets or boarding systems change seasonally. Permits for hiking Angels Landing are issued via a lottery system months in advance. State Parks like Snow Canyon have separate day-use fees; always check official NPS and Utah State Park sites for current access protocols.

days.title: Lava Tubes and Red Sandstone
days.start: Suggested: 7:30 AM from downtown St. George

stops.name: Snow Canyon State Park
stops.detail: Walk the Lava Flow Overlook trail to see ancient basalt and explore hidden volcanic tubes.

stops.name: Jenny’s Canyon
stops.detail: Hike this short, family-friendly slot canyon that leads to a scenic overlook.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes to the park entrance; conditions vary with seasonal wind.
days.note: Carry a headlamp if you plan to peer into the lava tubes.

days.title: Canyon Heights and River Trails
days.start: Suggested: 6 AM to reach Springdale gateway

stops.name: Temple of Sinawava
stops.detail: Access the gateway to The Narrows and walk along the Virgin River within Zion.

stops.name: Emerald Pools
stops.detail: Follow the trail to see desert oases and hanging gardens against red rock walls.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour to reach Zion; use the mandatory park shuttle within the canyon.
days.note: Parking at the Zion Visitor Center often fills by 8 AM; arrive early.

days.title: Desert Waters and Ancient Tracks

stops.name: Sand Hollow State Park
stops.detail: Experience the contrast of blue water against orange sand dunes at the reservoir.

stops.name: Dinosaur Discovery Site
stops.detail: See prehistoric tracks preserved in situ at this local paleontological museum.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes to Sand Hollow; local traffic in St. George is moderate.
days.note: Sand Hollow sand can be extremely hot; wear appropriate footwear on the dunes.

intel.title: Zion and State Park Caps
intel.text: Zion National Park parking is a major bottleneck; use the Springdale shuttle if the main lot is full. Snow Canyon lots are smaller; early morning arrival is advised to secure trail access.

intel.title: Remote Desert Gaps
intel.text: Expect strong signals in St. George city limits, but connectivity drops significantly inside Zion Canyon and remote areas of the Red Cliffs Reserve. Download offline navigation tools for hiking.

intel.title: Southwestern Hubs
intel.text: St. George and Hurricane are the primary fuel stops for this region. Do not enter the Kolob Canyons or Arizona Strip without a full tank, as services are non-existent.

intel.title: Heat and Flash Floods
intel.text: Monsoon season in late summer brings flash flood risks to slot canyons and The Narrows. Check the National Weather Service forecast daily before entering any narrow drainage.

intel.title: Permit Constraints
intel.text: Angels Landing access requires a specific permit through a lottery system; check the NPS site for seasonal deadlines. State parks may have temporary closures for trail maintenance or events.

plan.arrival: Fly into St. George Regional Airport (SGU) for a 24-minute drive to the city center, or arrive from Las Vegas (2 hours) for more rental options.
plan.vehicle: A standard car is perfect for paved park roads, but an OHV is required for exploring the dunes at Sand Hollow; check rental rules for off-road use.
plan.goldenHour: Dixie Rock (Sugarloaf) in Pioneer Park provides a 360-degree view of the city and red cliffs at sunset.
